key_insight: The paper proposes replacing objective-led trial and error with structure-driven solution construction whenever sufficient problem invariants are available.
engineering_relevance: Invariant-based mappings could support more interpretable solvers for constrained nonlinear engineering problems, with optimization retained when structure is insufficient.
method: Deconstruction: suspend prior assumptions and disentangle coupled components.
Structure and Construction: identify rigid invariants and build equivalent mappings anchored to them.
Solving: execute the mappings directly, then use metrics and experience for verification.
evidence_signal: The abstract cites demonstrations in number theory, Hamiltonian systems, deep learning, and seismic inversion, but reports no quantitative benchmarks or evaluation details.
watch_item: Practical value depends on reliably identifying sufficient invariants and establishing mapping equivalence; improved generalization remains unquantified in the abstract.
paper_title: The Four-Element Theory of Structure-Driven Methodology: A Methodological Shift from the Perspective of Natural Science and Engineering Practice
